novelty_flags.label: related_work; bibliography; literature checklist for ZhangZhao2026AverageCase
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited journal article labels the relevant optimizer result Proposition 3 and its average-case EIF result Theorem 1, not “Proposition 3.1” and “Theorem 4.1”; its Section 7 conclusion also does not state that longitudinal extension is left open.

soundness_flags.label: def:full-ray-inversion and thm:full-ray-breakdown

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper has Proposition 3 for the sensitivity-value optimizer, Theorem 1 for average-case EIFs, and §4.4 for multiplier bands; the conclusion discusses optimization relaxations and broader semiparametric applications rather than a stated longitudinal-extension open problem.

The article studies longitudinal time-varying treatments/covariates and gives observed-data convex-optimization representations for sharp and conservative bounds under primary, joint, and product sensitivity models.
The paper allows static or time-varying treatments and develops efficient estimators and confidence intervals for propensity-, outcome-, and subset-confounding MSM sensitivity models.
The published paper derives sharp ATE bounds under a bounded odds-ratio sensitivity model and proposes doubly-sharp/doubly-valid estimators.

DML uses orthogonal scores and cross-fitting; in smooth problems its crude sufficient nuisance requirement is o(n^-1/4), while its general conditions are expressed through intrinsic score-rate controls.
Preconstructed simultaneous confidence intervals yield simultaneous inner and outer confidence sets for inverse excursion sets with the SCI coverage probability.
The paper studies a binary-treatment breakdown frontier and develops lower uniform confidence bands, including monotonicity-based interpolation over a grid.
For Gaussian limits, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary bootstrap consistency; the paper gives an alternative resampling procedure for directionally differentiable maps.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the Zhang--Zhao anchors throughout: cite Proposition 3, Theorem 1, and §4.4 accurately, and replace the unsupported “Section 7 leaves longitudinal extension open” claim with the precise one-treatment-versus-two-treatment distinction.
Separate the original full-law ratio h0 from the projected observed-law ratio h0pr, then restate the projection lemma and compatible-law factorization using those distinct objects.
Define the generic inverse functional used by full-ray inversion and prove its deterministic coverage lemma before attaching the Gaussian endpoint-process theorem.

Add an explicit nondegenerate finite two-period law with both active prices and compute its two budget derivatives, so strict nonrepresentability by either comparator is exhibited rather than existential.
